id: title:Gilbert09:treat recursive rls policy errors as non retryable

review.posthog_relevance: PostHog warehouse ingestion workflows, specifically PostgreSQL RLS configuration recovery and connection management.
review.reason: Adds a non-retryable error classification for PostgreSQL row-level security policy recursion, potentially preventing retry loops and surfacing fixable errors. P1.F2.H1 adds tests, but P1.F1.H1 lacks the complete implementation and execution path, preventing a definitive tier assessment.
review.uncertainty: The chunk does not include the complete implementation or execution path, making it impossible to distinguish between a narrow maintenance change and a broader systemic improvement. The tier is assigned conservatively based on the observable addition of an error classification, while acknowledging the missing implementation details.

observations.limitations: This chunk does not include the complete implementation of the change. While P1.F1.H1 adds the error classification and P1.F2.H1 adds tests, the actual execution path and the complete implementation of the classification and message formatting are not shown. This prevents a definitive assessment of the tier.

observations.behavior: Adds a new non-retryable error classification for PostgreSQL row-level security policy recursion and its associated friendly message.
observations.posthog_connection: This could prevent PostHog warehouse ingestion workflows from entering a retry loop when encountering a specific PostgreSQL RLS configuration error, potentially recovering the connection or surfacing a fixable error instead of repeatedly failing.
